articles.title: Viral Dhokla Chaat Is the Diwali Party Starter You Need
articles.excerpt: Pooja Purohit's instant besan dhokla, steamed for 12-15 minutes and layered over yoghurt and chutneys with sev and pomegranate, gets a full chaat makeover for Diwali parties.
articles.image_caption: Dhokla
articles.nri_angle: A vegetarian, no-fry Diwali party starter diaspora hosts can batch-make from Indian-grocer staples and assemble to order for guests.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

steps: Take besan in a large mixing bowl. Add salt and turmeric powder.
Gradually pour in water while whisking to make a lump-free batter. Add oil and lemon juice and mix well.
Just before steaming, add Eno to the batter and gently mix until it becomes light and fluffy.
Grease dhokla moulds with oil. Pour the batter into them, filling each mould only about three-fourths of the way. Place them in a steamer and cook for around 12-15 minutes.
Heat oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add curry leaves and slit green chillies. Stir briefly and turn off the heat.
Remove the steamed dhokla from the moulds and place them on a plate. Pour the prepared tempering over them so that they absorb the flavours.
Take serving bowls and spread a layer of whisked yoghurt at the bottom. Add green chutney and tamarind chutney.
Place the steamed dhokla pieces over the yoghurt and chutneys. Sprinkle chaat masala and roasted cumin powder on top.
Garnish generously with sev, pomegranate pearls, boondi and freshly chopped coriander leaves.
Prepare the bowls just before serving so that the dhokla stays soft while the sev retains its crunch. Serve immediately.

articles.title: Kaju Katli for Diwali: Cashew, Sugar and Ghee, Cut Into Diamonds
articles.excerpt: The classic cashew fudge needs three ingredients and one judgement call — the one-string syrup. Two tested recipes, the powder method, and how long it keeps.
articles.image_caption: Kaju
articles.nri_angle: Every ingredient is available in a US supermarket: raw unsalted cashews, white sugar and ghee, with cardamom and optional silver leaf from an Indian grocery.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

steps: Powder the cashews in a dry mixer in one stretch. Do not grind too long — over-grinding makes the powder oily.
Boil the sugar with the water, stirring, until the syrup reaches one-string consistency: a drop stretched between finger and thumb forms a string that does not break.
Lower the flame completely and add the cashew powder, stirring continuously for 3 to 4 minutes until the mixture thickens and leaves the sides of the pan.
Test a tiny portion between greased fingers: you should be able to roll a soft, non-sticky ball.
Transfer the warm mixture to a greased tray or parchment and knead gently until the grainy dough turns smooth, sprinkling a little milk only if it is dry.
Roll into a thin layer and cut diagonally into diamond shapes. Cool completely before removing the pieces.
